Ophidian grotesques, I believe they're called?"<br />"Grotesque is certainly an accurate description.|[[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]] and [[Bevel Lemelisk]]|<ref name="Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut &mdash; The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref>}}
The '''ophidian grotesques''' were styles of design used in the most ancient districts of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. The grotesques were distinguished by sinuous patterns in their design, which were variously identified as [[Snake/Legends|snakes]], [[Vine/Legends|vines]], or [[Limb/Legends|tentacles]].

[[Pre-Republic era|Pre-Republic]] specialists like [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Insmot Bowen]] identified [[Sinuous carvings|recurring artistic motifs]] like the ophidian grotesques in ancient civilizations that were believed to have had contact with the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]]. Such motifs were also found on the worlds [[Caulus Tertius]] and [[Shatuun]], although these planets had been rendered uninhabitable in unknown cataclysms that Bowen believed were caused by the Celestials.

After [[Mission to the Maw|defeating]] the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] being [[Abeloth]] in [[44 ABY]], [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] investigated [[Ancient ruins (Abeloth's planet)|ancient ruins]] on [[Abeloth's planet]], where he found designs resembling the ophidian grotesques.
